questions.stem: What happens when COPY INTO runs again on a folder where some files were already loaded?

options.text: The table is dropped and recreated
Files already loaded are skipped, so the command can be rerun safely
Every file is loaded again, creating duplicates

questions.explanation: COPY INTO keeps track of loaded files and skips them on later runs, which makes it idempotent.

questions.stem: Which SQL command loads new CSV files from cloud storage into an existing Delta table?

options.text: COPY INTO sales FROM 's3://bucket/sales/' FILEFORMAT = CSV

questions.explanation: COPY INTO with a source path and FILEFORMAT loads files into a Delta table.

questions.stem: New CSV files have extra columns that the target table doesn't have yet. Which COPY INTO option lets the table schema grow to include them?

options.text: There's no way; COPY INTO never changes the schema

questions.explanation: With mergeSchema set to true, the target table's schema can evolve according to the incoming data.

questions.stem: You must reload files that COPY INTO already loaded once. Which option makes it load them again?
questions.explanation: With force set to true, idempotency is disabled and files are loaded whether or not they were loaded before.

questions.stem: When is COPY INTO a good fit compared with Auto Loader?

options.text: For continuously ingesting millions of files with schema evolution
For loading files in the thousands over time with a simple, rerunnable SQL command

questions.explanation: COPY INTO suits files in the order of thousands over time. For millions of files or more, Auto Loader is the recommended choice.
